card.name: Elections of presidents and incumbents
card.fires_on: Words about a head of state or incumbent being elected, re-elected, or voted against, in political or election news. It sits on the verb or title just before a party or office is likely to be named.

modes.label: Elected leader
modes.description: Verbs or dashes right after a president's name or the word president, about winning an election.
modes.example: President Armando Guebuza<< was>> elected in December 2004

modes.label: Incumbent and voters
modes.description: The word incumbent, or a voter-punishing verb, in talk of how voters treat the ruling side.
modes.example: voters often<< punish>> the incumbent party for adverse events

card.writes: It pushes the model toward the word party and away from appointment words like appoint and appointed.
card.plain: It marks election talk about presidents and incumbents, where the next word is likely to be party rather than appointed.
